title: The 1930 World Cup final's two balls
hook: The first World Cup final was played with two different balls, one each half.
peek: In 1930 Uruguay and Argentina met in Montevideo for the first World Cup final. Neither side would play with the other's ball, so they used one each. The score at half-time and full-time followed the ball.
lede: The first World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930, and the final, on 30 July in Montevideo, pitted the hosts against their neighbours Argentina. Footballs were not standard then, and each team wanted its own. The compromise was simple: Argentina's ball for the first half, Uruguay's for the second. Remarkably, each half went the way of the team whose ball was in play.

bullets.text: With their ball, Argentina came from behind to lead 2-1 at half-time. Their forward Guillermo Stábile, the tournament's top scorer, got one of the goals.
With the Uruguayan ball, which was reportedly larger and heavier, the hosts scored three times without reply. Uruguay won 4-2 and became the first world champions.
The final was played in the Estadio Centenario, built for the tournament and named for the centenary of Uruguay's first constitution. It is still in use today.
Thousands of Argentine supporters crossed the River Plate by boat for the final. The Belgian referee, John Langenus, agreed to take charge only at the last minute.
